prompt: Name a feature film Steven Spielberg directed in the 2000s or later.

answers.name: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
answers.fact: Released nineteen years after the previous Indiana Jones film — the longest gap between any two entries in the series.

answers.name: Minority Report
answers.fact: The gesture interface was designed by consultants who later built real versions of it.

answers.name: War of the Worlds
answers.fact: Made quickly after Wells' novel had sat with Spielberg since childhood.

answers.name: Catch Me If You Can
answers.fact: Based on Frank Abagnale's account of himself, much of which has since been questioned.

answers.name: Ready Player One
answers.fact: The film rights sold before Ernest Cline's novel was even published, in 2011.

answers.name: Lincoln
answers.fact: Daniel Day-Lewis based the voice on descriptions of it as reedy and high, not sonorous.

answers.name: A.I. Artificial Intelligence
answers.fact: Inherited from Stanley Kubrick, who had developed it for years before his death.

answers.name: West Side Story
answers.fact: His first musical, made at 74, with no subtitles on the Spanish dialogue by design.

answers.name: The Fabelmans
answers.fact: A version of his own childhood and his parents' divorce.

answers.name: The Terminal
answers.fact: Loosely inspired by Mehran Karimi Nasseri, who lived for years in Charles de Gaulle airport.

answers.name: War Horse
answers.fact: Adapted from the stage play, and shot on Dartmoor.

answers.name: Bridge of Spies
answers.fact: The Coen brothers rewrote the script.

answers.name: Munich
answers.fact: Written by Tony Kushner, who went on to write Lincoln and West Side Story for him.

answers.name: The Adventures of Tintin
answers.fact: His only animated feature, made with performance capture alongside Peter Jackson.

answers.name: The BFG
answers.fact: Adapted from Roald Dahl, with Mark Rylance in a motion-capture role — one of Spielberg's rare outright box-office flops.
